questions.q: Which species does NOT act as an electrophile?
questions.explain: NH₄⁺ is positively charged, but its nitrogen has a complete octet and no vacant orbital, so it cannot accept an electron pair. BF₃ and the carbene have incomplete octets, and NO₂⁺ is a cationic electrophile.

questions.q: Which of the following is an ambident nucleophile?
questions.explain: Nitrite can attack through O (giving R–ONO) or through N (giving R–NO₂). Carbonate is the trap: its three donor atoms are equivalent oxygens, so all attacks give the same product.

questions.q: Which species can act as a nucleophile?
questions.explain: Benzene donates its loosely held π electrons to electrophiles, which is why it undergoes electrophilic substitution. AlCl₃ and BH₃ have incomplete octets and Ag⁺ is a metal cation: all three are electrophiles.

questions.q: An alkyl halide R–X is treated separately with KNO₂ and with AgNO₂. The main products are, respectively,
questions.explain: Ionic KNO₂ gives a free nitrite ion that attacks through the O atom, forming the alkyl nitrite R–O–N=O; with AgNO₂ the attack is through N, giving the nitroalkane R–NO₂.
